project.name: docmonstakrakin
project.description: Agentic Secure Software Development Life Cycle (A-SSDLC) development control plane providing deterministic governance, risk management, threat modeling, architecture ratification, and verifiable technical evidence tracking.
project.deploymentIntent: Local-first web application / local application service with offline-capable project state

productBaseline.problemStatement: Autonomous and semi-autonomous AI coding agents introduce critical security and governance risks: unvetted architecture decisions, vulnerability amplification, lack of verifiable lineage between requirements and code, and unverified task completion claims.
targetUsers: Autonomous and Semi-Autonomous AI Coding Agents
coreCapabilities: Deterministic 15-phase A-SSDLC lifecycle state machine and human approval gates
Single canonical project state model with deterministic artifact projections
Evidence-backed technical verification and cryptographic audit chaining
Dual-agent independent cross-review orchestration and prompt compilation
Local-first, offline-capable project management and fail-closed secrets security
coreFeatures: Lifecycle Phase Machine & Deterministic Risk Floors
Scoped Context Package Compiler & Structured Proposal Validation
Unified WorkItem Engine (WBS, Kanban, Backlog Projections)
Repository Command Safety & Path Traversal Interceptor
Cryptographic Evidence Chaining & Requirements Traceability Matrix
Encrypted Local SecretStore with OS Keychain Fallback
primaryWorkflows: Risk Assessment & Threat Modeling with Mandatory Floors
Scoped Prompt Context Compilation & AI Agent Proposal Review
Work Item Implementation & Cryptographic Evidence Attachment
Human Quorum Review & Release Gate Evaluation
nonGoals: Direct autonomous code execution without human approval
Commercial subscription billing and tenant management
Direct automated cloud production deployment pipelines
Generic AI chat wrapper or prompt playground
successCriteria: 100% referential integrity across requirements, architecture, risks, work items, and evidence
Zero unauthenticated or synthetic approval injection during governance evaluation
Full offline capability for local project control and verification workflows
Zero secret leakage into plain-text logs, audits, or portable exports

requirements.title: Canonical Project State Aggregate
requirements.statement: The system must maintain exactly one canonical in-memory project aggregate model from which all views (Kanban, WBS, PRD, RTM) are deterministically projected.
requirements.rationale: Eliminates state synchronization drift across disparate views and task trackers.

requirements.title: Optimistic Concurrency & State Versioning
requirements.statement: All project mutations must increment a strictly monotonic stateVersion counter and reject conflicting writes using optimistic locking.
requirements.rationale: Prevents lost updates during rapid asynchronous UI and agent state mutations.

requirements.title: Field-level Data Masking for Sensitive PII
requirements.statement: Export and display pipelines must automatically redact registered secrets, private keys, and sensitive PII tokens prior to serialization.
requirements.rationale: Prevents accidental leakage of proprietary and sensitive credentials.

requirements.title: Standalone Portable Project Package Envelope
requirements.statement: The system must support packaging complete project state into a portable cryptographic archive (.docmonstakrakin) with sealed checksums.
requirements.rationale: Enables reproducible offline project transfer and archival across workstations.

requirements.title: Conditional Questionnaire Dependency Graph
requirements.statement: Requirements discovery must evaluate dynamic answer state and conditional branching rules across 19 technical domains without deadlocks.
requirements.rationale: Guides users through tailored architectural discovery based on selected project profiles.

requirements.title: Deterministic 15-Phase Lifecycle Gate Enforcement
requirements.statement: Transition between any of the 15 A-SSDLC lifecycle phases must strictly require passing deterministic entry and exit criteria.
requirements.rationale: Prevents premature advancement to implementation or release before requirements and architecture are verified.

requirements.title: Auditable Gate Overrides with Expiration
requirements.statement: Authorized operators may override gate blockers only with recorded rationale, acknowledged residual risk, and bounded expiration timestamp.
requirements.rationale: Provides emergency engineering flexibility while preserving non-repudiable audit trails.

requirements.title: Mandatory Risk Floors for Dangerous Capabilities
requirements.statement: Projects declaring autonomous agent execution, production secret handling, or safety-critical data must enforce non-negotiable risk floor minimums.
requirements.rationale: Prevents artificial downgrade of inherent risks associated with high-impact attack surfaces.

requirements.title: Single-Use Password Reset & Token Expiry (T <= 900s)
requirements.statement: Authentication tokens and password reset credentials must enforce single-use consumption and absolute expiration within 900 seconds.
requirements.rationale: Mitigates token replay, credential theft, and unauthorized session resurrection.

requirements.title: Concurrent Session Anomaly & Refresh-Token Revocation
requirements.statement: Session manager must detect concurrent anomalous logins, invalidate compromised refresh token families, and alert the security officer.
requirements.rationale: Protects against hijacked session tokens and unauthorized administrative access.

requirements.title: Server-Side AI Inference Gateway & Token Isolation
requirements.statement: All AI provider API interactions must execute server-side in an isolated adapter; client browser bundles must never receive raw API keys.
requirements.rationale: Isolates model credentials and enforces strict egress filtering to approved AI endpoints.

requirements.title: Independent Dual-Agent Cross-Review Orchestration
requirements.statement: High-risk AI proposals must undergo cross-review by an independent secondary agent without shared context scratchpads prior to human review.
requirements.rationale: Counters sycophantic model confirmation bias and catches subtle hallucinations in code proposals.

requirements.title: Workspace Path Boundary & Command Sandbox Policy
requirements.statement: The system must enforce strict canonical workspace boundary assertions and command policy allow/deny masks for all agent operations.
requirements.rationale: Prevents directory traversal escapes and unvetted destructive command execution on the host machine.

requirements.title: v0.1 Definition-of-Done Release Gate Verification
requirements.statement: Gate 7 release sign-off must require 100% verification across all blocking requirements, clean test regressions, and human cryptographic sign-off.
requirements.rationale: Guarantees release integrity and prevents unverified promotions to production.

requirements.title: CryptoDemon Security & Isolation Fixture Verification
requirements.statement: The system must verify project state isolation, zero requirement leakage, and neutral technology defaults under the CryptoDemon fixture.
requirements.rationale: Ensures that projects remain completely isolated with clean discovery boundaries.

requirements.title: Reviewer Authentication, Quorum & ADR Immutability Controls
requirements.statement: Human reviewer authentication must require distinct authenticated identities for quorum slots, enforce HttpOnly sessions, and preserve accepted ADR immutability.
requirements.rationale: Prevents reviewer impersonation, self-approval bypass, and silent tampering of accepted architectural decisions.

requirements.title: Full Technical Regression, Drift & Build Assurance
requirements.statement: The codebase must maintain 100% green pass rates across all 22 test suites, zero WBS drift, 93 automated acceptance criteria, and clean production builds.
requirements.rationale: Ensures technical integrity and prevents regression before release candidate handoff.

requirements.title: Structured Proposal Contract Schema 1.1 Ingestion Verification
requirements.statement: Proposal ingestion must validate Schema 1.1 contracts across CREATE/MODIFY/DELETE modes with complete error indexing and sanitize malformed prose.
requirements.rationale: Guarantees fail-closed validation of candidate artifacts proposed by external AI agents.

requirements.title: Trusted Self-Bootstrap Initialization Contract
requirements.statement: The system must provide deterministic validation and ingestion of the PRJ-DOCMONSTAKRAKIN self-bootstrap manifest without synthetic governance injection.
requirements.rationale: Enables docmonstakrakin to transition from hardcoded seed state to self-governed canonical project state.

requirements.title: Projects Workspace & Reliable Project Switching
requirements.statement: The UI console must allow operators to switch cleanly between distinct local projects with full isolation and zero cross-project cache leakage.
requirements.rationale: Allows operators to manage both docmonstakrakin self-governance and external projects seamlessly.

requirements.title: Controlled Repository Documentation Workspace
requirements.statement: The system must render repository-controlled markdown and YAML documents in-console, verifying live SHA-256 digests against registered baseline hashes.
requirements.rationale: Maintains alignment between executable code, control documents, and architectural baselines.

requirements.title: Formal Requirement Sign-Off UX (Batch 2)
requirements.statement: The governance console must provide explicit, interactive requirement approval workflows with authenticated human sign-off logging.
requirements.rationale: Enables formal human approval of individual requirements during lifecycle phase reviews.

requirements.title: Approval Inbox & Distinct Human Quorum Synchronization (Batch 3)
requirements.statement: The UI must expose an Approval Inbox requiring distinct human authenticated roles to satisfy multi-party governance quorums.
requirements.rationale: Guarantees dual-signoff separation of duty for security and architecture approvals.

requirements.title: Reviewer Provisioning & Governance Setup UX (Batch 4)
requirements.statement: The application must provide operator-facing UI to manage local reviewer rosters, assign security roles, and rotate credentials securely.
requirements.rationale: Simplifies secure reviewer onboarding without exposing plaintext credential configuration files.

adrs.title: Local-First In-Memory & Storage Architecture
adrs.author: Lead Architect, Project Lead
adrs.context: docmonstakrakin is designed as an offline-first engineering cockpit for local developers and autonomous coding agents. Relying on external cloud databases introduces latency, cloud failure modes, and credential exposure risks.
adrs.decision: We decide to maintain project state in an in-memory aggregate backed by atomic local file persistence and encrypted OS keychains.

positive: Sub-millisecond local reads and UI responsiveness
Zero cloud telemetry leakage or vendor lock-in
Complete offline operational capability
negative: Memory footprint scales with project size
Requires explicit file locking and atomic swap routines for persistence
risks: Unsaved mutations lost if process crashes without write-flush

adrs.title: Single Canonical WorkItem Aggregate Model
adrs.author: Lead Architect, Project Lead
adrs.context: Task tracking is frequently fractured across Kanban boards, WBS sheets, and PR checklists, causing synchronization drift and phantom completion claims.
adrs.decision: We decide that the system will maintain exactly one canonical WorkItem aggregate model. Kanban, WBS, Product Backlog, and Sprint views are deterministic projections.

positive: Zero state drift between Kanban cards and WBS hierarchy
Status updates instantly project across all views
Traceability links attach directly to the single canonical entity
negative: WorkItem schema must accommodate diverse view attributes
risks: Overly complex WorkItem schema if view-specific concerns are not segregated

adrs.title: Sandboxed Server-Side AI Inference Adapter & Egress Boundary
adrs.author: Security Officer, Lead Architect
adrs.context: Calling AI models directly from browser code exposes API keys, allows untrusted payload execution, and induces sycophantic self-review bias.
adrs.decision: We mandate server-side AI inference exclusively, strict egress whitelisting (*.googleapis.com), and independent dual-agent cross-review for high-risk proposals.

positive: API keys never touch the browser DOM or client storage
Mitigates prompt injection secret exfiltration
Catches subtle model hallucinations and sycophancy
negative: Requires server proxy overhead for streaming connections
risks: Provider rate limits or API outages stall AI-assisted workflows

adrs.title: Cryptographic Hash-Chained Audit Ledger
adrs.author: Security Officer, Project Lead
adrs.context: Standard log files can be edited or truncated by malicious scripts or compromised agents to hide unvetted actions or gate bypasses.
adrs.decision: We implement an append-only, cryptographically hash-chained audit ledger where each event hashes its predecessor: Hash_n = SHA-256(Event_n || Hash_n-1).

positive: Non-repudiation for all gate transitions and overrides
Complete tamper evidence without blockchain overhead
Provable audit history exportable offline
negative: Requires strict deterministic canonical JSON serialization prior to hashing
risks: Ledger corruption if events are appended without proper synchronization

adrs.title: Synchronization Protocol and Conflict Resolution Model
adrs.author: Lead Architect, Security Officer
adrs.context: Supporting multi-workstation collaboration in future milestones requires robust offline synchronization without losing human governance authority.
adrs.decision: Candidate recommendation: Hybrid Local-First 3-Way Semantic Merge + Merkle DAG Ledger with zero-knowledge encrypted transport.

positive: Preserves local write speed and offline capability
Zero-knowledge relay isolation protects project confidentiality
Human governance approvals cannot be overwritten by agent writes
negative: Complex 3-way merge logic required for semantic conflict handling
risks: Divergent branches require manual operator reconciliation

adrs.title: Multi-Agent Peer Identity and Trust Boundary Model
adrs.author: Security Officer, Lead Architect
adrs.context: Distinguishing autonomous AI agents from human project owners is critical to prevent automated bypass of human-in-the-loop governance.
adrs.decision: Candidate recommendation: Cryptographic Ed25519 Peer Keyring with Scoped Delegation Agent Keys; agent keys rejected for Gate Sign-off.

positive: Cryptographic separation of human authority vs agent capability
Decentralized peer identity without corporate directory lock-in
Scoped delegation prevents privilege escalation
negative: Requires local keypair management and signing ceremonies
risks: Loss of private key requires multi-owner recovery ceremony

adrs.title: Deterministic Self-Bootstrap Ingestion Contract
adrs.author: Security Officer & Lead Architect
adrs.context: Adopting the SELF_BOOTSTRAP_V1 specification to populate the authoritative project state for PRJ-DOCMONSTAKRAKIN without executing runtime mutation during contract verification, eliminating circular dependencies between dogfooding control and project creation.
adrs.decision: Implement a deterministic, closed-schema self-bootstrap contract with strict referential integrity, sensitive key scanning, recursive governance checks, and canonical JSON SHA-256 hashing.

positive: Guarantees deterministic project onboarding
Prevents unvetted governance injection
Enables reproducible offline verification
negative: Requires rigid schema adherence with zero arbitrary extensions
risks: Malformed manifest rejection halts self-bootstrap until manually corrected
